name: serverexternalpackages-vs-webpackconfig-externals
hook: serverExternalPackages prevents Next.js serverless bundling; webpackConfig.externals prevents webpack from analyzing a package's internals
body: serverExternalPackages tells the Next.js build system to leave a package out of the serverless function bundle (loaded from node_modules at runtime). But webpack still analyzes the package's source when bundling the app code that imports it — for tree-shaking, dead code elimination, etc. webpackConfig.externals tells webpack to treat the package as an external Node.js module and skip all source analysis. Both are needed: serverExternalPackages for the bundler output, webpackConfig.externals for preventing webpack from encountering node: imports during analysis.
why: node-fetch was in serverExternalPackages (correctly, to reduce bundle size) but NOT in webpackConfig.externals. Webpack still analyzed node-fetch's internals for tree-shaking, encountered node:https/node:http/node:net/node:dns imports, and threw UnhandledSchemeError.

name: resolve-alias-handles-node-protocol-prefixed-modules
hook: resolve.alias CAN intercept node: protocol imports when module name includes the 'node:' prefix
body: webpack resolve.alias operates on the module request string. If a file does require('node:fs'), the module name is 'node:fs' and resolve.alias['node:fs'] correctly redirects it. The previous session's lesson said 'resolve.alias cannot intercept node: protocol' — that was wrong. The correct statement is: resolve.alias cannot intercept bare 'fs' when the code uses require('node:fs') AND the package is not in externals. But when the request IS 'node:fs', resolve.alias['node:fs'] works. The node: protocol prefix makes the module name include 'node:' so alias can match it.
why: The previous fix (2476) used resolve.alias entries for node:console etc. but also removed externals — so webpack still analyzed undici which then had node:dns in mock utils, not via require('node:dns') directly. Now with externals AND resolve.alias together, we have defense in depth: externals prevents analysis entirely, and alias stubs any remaining node: references webpack does analyze.
